subject: SablePoint SLA breach — consolidated RCA, mitigation timeline & owner roster
messages:
From: Rajesh Mehra <rajesh.mehra@sablepoint.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: SablePoint Ops <ops@sablepoint.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 429s impacting inference pipelines (SablePoint)

Camila —

We started seeing sharp increases in latency and a significant number of 429/503 responses for our inference requests to the Redwood hosted endpoint starting ~14:30 PDT. This is impacting our live ranking pipeline — errors spike when batch sizes exceed our usual 8 requests. We attached a short HAR and a sample error log.

Impact: ~25% of requests returning throttling errors, median latency up from 120ms -> 920ms across several keys. Our retry logic is hitting downstream backoffs and causing downstream queueing.

Can we get immediate mitigation steps and an ETA for a permanent fix? We are in the middle of a customer demo tomorrow and this is high severity for us.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Sr. Platform Engineer — SablePoint

Attachments: sablepoint_har_20270524.har (referenced), sablepoint_error_sample.log

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Mehra <rajesh.mehra@sablepoint.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:10:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 429s impacting inference pipelines (SablePoint)

On the call we confirmed the pattern: a combination of a sudden increase in peak concurrent short-lived connections from SablePoint's batcher + a routing rule that kept sending traffic to a GPU pool operating near capacity for the 8k token variant.

Short-term mitigations applied (15:55 PDT):
- Enabled temporary soft-throttling on SablePoint API key to smooth bursts (reduced retries).
- Rerouted large-batch traffic to an alternate model variant with higher throughput for sequences <2k tokens (routing rule change).
- Increased per-second token token-burst window for the affected pool by +20% to absorb remaining inflight.

Observed effect: error rate fell from ~25% to ~3% within 10 minutes, median latency returned to ~180–240ms for most routes. Operational monitoring is green but we'll keep elevated alerting for 48 hours.

Pending items we committed to while triaging:
1) Full RCA with root cause analysis and kernel-level profile (due EOD Tuesday 2027-05-25).
2) Backfill of missing telemetry for the 14:30–15:30 window and a consolidated log bundle (shared to Drive).
3) Recommendations for long-term routing / autoscale policy changes and a pre-approved burst capacity plan.

Neha — please start a mitigation runbook draft and capture the exact kernel/quantization variant used by the affected pool.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Please add an explicit owner for the long-term changes (routing policy review, autoscale tuning, and signal enrichment). I want names and dates.

Camila — can you confirm we have buy-in from SablePoint on the burst-capacity plan and whether they'd accept a temporary credit for SLA exposure? Procurement may escalate otherwise.

I'll be available to call out any cross-org blockers.

Markus
